propositions: Detached pytest runs report test failures and errors that do not reproduce in foreground runs, appearing to be regressions but caused by concurrent external mutations of the checkout while the suite runs.

The `_no_repo_root_leaks` autouse fixture cannot distinguish between test-induced and externally-caused mutations of REPO_ROOT, and misattributes external writes to innocent tests while deleting the external files.
Browser e2e test failures triggered by signal-killed child processes report empty stderr without inspecting returncode, making signal termination indistinguishable from genuine product failures.

The guard message 'Test leaked new entries into REPO_ROOT' asserts a falsehood when a concurrent external actor creates entries, and provides no information about the child's death signal when a process is killed.

A detached run enables concurrent external actors (git commits, file writes, process reaps) that cannot occur during a blocking foreground run, making detachment an enabler of the real cause rather than the cause itself.
Guidance on trustworthy local-tree validation methods, including detached vs. foreground tradeoffs and worktree isolation, is entirely undocumented.
